column1: # Per-function CALL COUNT comparison, port vs C, on byte-identical still-frame
# encodes — the measurement docs/WORKING-ON-THIS.md and the campaign brief
# asked for after perf_still_attrib_2026-09-03 found the still-path gap is
# NOT SIMD (SIMD_GAP was the smallest bucket, 5-11%) and asked whether the
# port is doing repeated/extra work rather than the same work more slowly.
#   a32d82e82, the last code-touching commit; c4ff4727 is docs-only)
# host=r7900x (x86_64-linux, AMD, 24 cores), unpushed-locally commit is
#   docs-only (CHANGELOG.md) so it does not affect anything measured here.
# cells: gradient 512x512 qp 40, presets 2 / 6 / 10, STILL config
#   (no SVTAV1_VIDEO) — the three cells perf_still_attrib_2026-09-03 uses,
#   so these numbers join that record. warmup=0 (one init+encode cycle,
#   both sides) so call counts are NOT diluted by an extra warmup pass.
# byte-identity: VERIFIED for all 6 runs (3 presets x {port,C}) via
#   `cmp` against a same-session, non-callgrind identity pre-pass AND
#   against the callgrind-run output itself — see callcount_2026-09-04.meta.
# METHOD: callgrind_annotate does not summarize invocation counts (only Ir
#   callgrind ASCII format directly and sums every `calls=N` edge into each
#   callee, giving total times-called. Edge-level (caller->callee) counts
#   and their inclusive Ir cost/share come from
#   c_site      C function (or caller->callee edge), with file:line where load-bearing
#   c_count     C total call count (or edge call count) for this preset
#   port_site   port function (or caller->callee edge), with file:line
#   port_count  port total call count (or edge call count) for this preset
#   ratio       port_count / c_count  ("no_c_edge" when C has zero calls on this edge)
